Over time, fungi evolved to occupy a range of ecological roles, including intertwined relationships with plants. Many plants can't survive without these fungal partners. Other fungi evolved remarkable strategies to defend against, exploit, and manipulate their neighbors, often by producing an arsenal of compounds like antibiotics, toxins, and even psychedelics.
